title: Verify OptiSweep/WCS Windows service health when RMS/logs appear silent
summary: When the system appears to have a crash/restart period and logs may be silent, verify whether the relevant OptiSweep/WCS Windows service(s) are actually Running vs Stopped in the Windows Services MMC. Use the service state as the primary observable when log activity is missing.
when_to_use: Use when RMS and/or other log-based signals appear silent during a suspected OptiSweep/WCS crash/restart window, and you need host-level evidence that the service is Running vs Stopped.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Check Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host to confirm whether OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Running vs Stopped, and escalate if the relevant service(s) cannot be identified or the status is unclear.
access_or_tools_needed: Windows Services MMC / Windows Services view (event_viewer surface)

access_required: Windows Services MMC access on the OptiSweep/WCS host
system_preconditions: You are investigating a suspected crash/restart period where logs may be silent

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the segment discussion that during a crash the service must stop and logs may be silent; it also mentions checking Windows Services and that there are about 10 services.

steps.title: Open Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host
steps.purpose: Establish the host-level view needed to determine whether the OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Running vs Stopped when logs may be silent.
steps.instruction: On the OptiSweep/WCS host, open the Windows Services MMC / Windows Services view (the Services list).
steps.expected_result: The Services list is visible with a Status column that can show Running vs Stopped for services.
steps.healthy_condition: You can clearly see the Services list and the Status values (Running/Stopped) for services.
steps.failure_condition: The Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, or you cannot access the Services MMC on the host.

actions.label: Open Services MMC
actions.exact_action: Open the Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host.

stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot access the Windows Services MMC on the OptiSweep/WCS host

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “It’s a Windows… you check the service services… there are 10 services.”

steps.title: Locate OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check Running vs Stopped
steps.purpose: Determine whether the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Running or Stopped during the suspected silent/crash window.
steps.instruction: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) (the segment notes there are about 10 services) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.
steps.expected_result: You identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and observe their Status as Running or Stopped.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running during normal operation.
steps.failure_condition: The OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped, or you observe restart behavior consistent with the suspected crash/restart period.

actions.label: Find relevant services and read Status
actions.exact_action: In the Services list, locate the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) and check the Status column for Running vs Stopped.

stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list
The Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “the service must stop” and “the log will be silent” and “how will someone support… know that service is just gone… It’s a Windows… you check the service services… there are 10 services.”

steps.title: Interpret Stopped/restarting service state as evidence consistent with the silent crash window
steps.purpose: Use the service state as the observable indicator when logs are silent, matching the segment’s described behavior during crash periods.
steps.instruction: If the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) are Stopped (or show restart behavior), treat that as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period during the suspected crash window.
steps.expected_result: Your conclusion matches the observed Status: Stopped/restarting supports the suspected crash/restart period; Running supports normal operation.
steps.healthy_condition: During normal operation, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Running.
steps.failure_condition: During the suspected crash window, the OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) are Stopped or restarting.

actions.label: Confirm evidence from service state
actions.exact_action: If the service is Stopped (or repeatedly restarting), treat this as evidence consistent with the segment’s “service must stop” / “service was just like … gone” period.

stop_or_escalate_if: You cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “except the service from the service must stop. Service must stop right… the log will be silent… you check the service services… there are 10 services.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate when service identification/status is unclear
steps.purpose: Ensure you do not proceed with an unsupported conclusion when the relevant service(s) cannot be identified or the status evidence is not clear.
steps.instruction: If you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list, or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status, stop and escalate.
steps.expected_result: Escalation is initiated with the evidence that the relevant service(s) could not be identified or status was unclear.
steps.healthy_condition: The relevant service(s) are identifiable and show clear Running/Stopped status.
steps.failure_condition: Service identification is ambiguous or the Services view does not provide clear Running/Stopped status.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if you cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) in the Services list or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.

stop_or_escalate_if: Cannot identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS service(s) among the ~10 services
Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “there are 10 services” and the segment’s stated challenge is knowing the service is gone when logs are silent by checking Windows Services.

success_criteria: You can identify the relevant OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) in the Windows Services MMC and observe clear Status values (Running vs Stopped).
During the suspected crash window, the observed service state (Stopped/restarting) aligns with the segment’s described “service must stop” / “logs may be silent” behavior.
healthy_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Running in the Windows Services MMC during normal operation.
failure_conditions: OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show Status = Stopped during the suspected crash window.
OptiSweep/WCS-related service(s) show restart behavior consistent with an unplanned crash/restart period.
Relevant service(s) cannot be identified among the ~10 services, or Running/Stopped status is unclear.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if you cannot map which of the ~10 services corresponds to the affected component or if the Services view does not show clear Running/Stopped status.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Transcript: “It’s a Windows… you check the service services… there are 10 services.” Also: “the service must stop” and logs may be silent.

missing_details: The segment does not name specific OptiSweep/WCS service names; the runbook therefore cannot provide a deterministic mapping from “affected component” to a specific service name beyond using the Services list to identify the relevant service(s).
